papers.title: Cell-type-resolved methylation analysis using bulk long-read sequencing across human tissues
papers.abstract: DNA methylation shapes cellular identity and changes with aging and disease, but most human methylomes come from bulk tissue, which mixes signal across many cell types. A methylation change at the bulk tissue level can reflect a change in cellular composition or an intrinsic shift within a cell type, and the two cannot be separated from bulk data. Single-cell and sorted-cell methods resolve cell types directly, but their cost and workflow complexity pose challenges to large studies. Long-read sequencing of single DNA molecules can directly detect DNA methylation on each read. We built COMET (Cell-of-Origin from METhylation), a framework that uses cell-type-specific methylation to assign individual long reads to cell types from standard bulk long-read sequencing. COMET detects changes in cell-type composition robustly even from shallow bulk long-read data, quantifies methylation level of repetitive DNA within each cell type, and, with deeper sequencing, resolves methylation differences between health and disease in individual cell types. We applied COMET to 140 human blood samples, 104 human brain samples and 59 human colon samples. In blood, we found epigenetic aging clock is primarily driven by shifts in cell-type composition, and that APOE4 carriers have myeloid-specific methylation changes. In brain, we found sex-biased change in cell-type composition with age, resolved methylation and hydroxymethylation separately within each cell type. In colon, we found a consistent expansion of fibroblasts in tumors relative to matched normal tissue, localized methylation loss at LINE-1 in fibroblast cells, and identified tumor- and cell-type-specific hypermethylation in epithelial cells at the promoters of known colorectal cancer genes. By resolving cell-type-specific methylation directly from bulk long-read data, this approach opens broad study of cell-type epigenetics across human tissues in aging and disease.

papers.title: Apples-to-apples transcriptomics: a parent-of-origin-resolved 'Granny Smith' genome reveals how reference choice shapes biological interpretation
papers.abstract: The accuracy and reliability of RNA-seqbased transcriptome profiling inherently depends on how well the reference genome represents the genotype being studied, particularly in highly heterozygous, clonally propagated crops with many genetically distinct cultivars, such as apple. Here, we present a chromosome-scale, parent-of-origin-resolved genome assembly and highly complete annotation for Granny Smith (assembly BUSCO = 98.6% both haplotypes; annotation BUSCO = 98.7-98.9%). To test how reference genome choice influences transcriptomic interpretation, we mapped RNA-seq data from sun- and shade-exposed Granny Smith peel independently to three different apple genome references: GDDH13 (earlier-generation), WA 38 (modern-generation), and both Granny Smith haplotypes (modern and cultivar matched). Despite small difference in unique mapping rate, transcriptome analysis using the modern references showed greater agreement in differentially expressed gene families than GDDH13, while the cultivar-matched Granny Smith references recovered additional functional responses associated with oxidative stress, cuticle biology, and other processes relevant to sun exposure and cold storage. Importantly, many responses were consistent with previously identified metabolomic patterns from the same experimental material, providing independent biological support for signals recovered with the matched reference. Reference-dependent differences were greatest for the subtle sun-exposure storage interaction, indicating reference limitations become more consequential as biological contrasts become finer. Orthogroup-based analyses further showed that both reference-generation differences and paralog representation contribute to cross-genome disagreement. Together, these results demonstrate that seemingly modest differences in mapping performance can substantially alter biological conclusions and highlight the value of high-quality, genotype-matched references for resolving cultivar-specific stress and postharvest physiology in heterozygous perennial crops.

papers.title: AMBER: mapping accessible chromatin associations through barcode seed expansion
papers.abstract: Accessible chromatin establishes higher-order regulatory structures spanning multiple spatial scales. We developed AMBER, a hydrogel-assisted approach for confined expansion of barcode seeds and subsequent recording of accessible chromatin associations. In mouse brain cells, we characterized the multi-scale regulatory organizations that accessibility alone cannot explain. We identified a subset of genomic regions enriched for inter-chromosomal interactions that also encode proteins engaged in interaction networks. These regulatory hubs are essential for neural function and help predict disease-risk loci and regulators.

papers.title: Spatial and epigenetic programs underlie heterogeneous cellular senescence in the aging liver
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process leading to tissue dysfunction, and driven in part by progressive epigenetic drift, widespread transcriptional dysregulation and cellular senescence. Senescent cells (SnCs) accumulate across tissues in a heterogeneous and cell type-specific manner, yet their molecular signatures and spatial organization within native tissue have not been systematically mapped. Here we combined single-nucleus transcriptomic, epigenomic, three-dimensional (3D) genome and spatial profiling to systematically characterize aging of the mouse liver and associated cellular senescence. Aging was marked by hepatocyte loss, immune cell expansion, erosion of repressive H3K9me3 heterochromatin, alteration of 3D genome organization, and activation of stress-response pathways known to promote senescence. Age-associated SnCs were spatially colocalized within discrete inflammatory microenvironments termed SenSpots. Different SenSpots were dominated by distinct hepatocyte senescence states (senotypes), driven by unique transcription factors, and exhibited distinct lobular zonation. Single-cell DNA methylation profiling revealed a subset of immune cells in aged livers with loss of DNA methylation at constitutive heterochromatin and elevated senescence signatures. AAV-mediated, p21-promoter driven Stat1 deletion in the aged liver selectively suppressed interferon-responsive senescence programs while pharmacological inhibition of MDM2 attenuated senescence-associated inflammatory signatures. Together, these findings reveal that hepatic senescence is not a uniform state but a set of diverse epigenetically reprogrammed, spatially organized, and pharmacologically modifiable inflammatory niches.

papers.title: Generation of a Public Dataset for Etiological Subtyping with the Genomic Cluster Engine
papers.abstract: Motivation: Genetic diseases are complex phenomena that are currently defined by their clinical symptoms, rather than by the combinations of variants that give rise to them. Incomplete penetrance and phenotypic variability indicate that the genomic background contributes to the effect of variants. Recent advancements in genomics have produced vast amounts of data and created new opportunities to study genetic diversity across human populations. Much of this variation is inherited as recombination-defined contiguous segments, called haploblocks. We previously introduced a novel methodology for genomic hash encoding, the Genomic Cluster Engine, which groups individuals into clusters using phased haploblock sequences. By encoding each haploblock sequence as a compact hash, the characterization of genomic backgrounds, the subtyping of etiologies and the inference of local ancestry become fast and scalable. Results: We have optimized the Genomic Cluster Engine pipeline for large genomic datasets through parallelization and improved memory management. We applied our pipeline to 2,548 individuals across 26 populations from the 1000 Genomes Project and produced a dataset of haploblock-based genomic hashes for the resulting clusters. The genomic hashes and clusters can be used for investigating variant effects in the context of their haplotype backgrounds or for genotype-phenotype association studies. This comprehensive dataset is now publicly available, providing a valuable resource for both academic and industry researchers worldwide. Availability: The haploblock boundaries, sequences, clusters and genomic hashes for the 1000 Genomes Project are available under the CC0 license at https://data.haploblocks.org and on the Registry of Open Data on AWS https://registry.opendata.aws.

papers.title: Disentangling genomic imprinting from indirect parental genetic effects on the human methylome
papers.abstract: Imprinted genes regulate development and metabolism and are implicated in both rare developmental syndromes and common diseases. Genomic imprinting is conventionally inferred from parent-of-origin effects (POEs), identified as differences between heterozygotes who inherited an allele from their mother and those who inherited it from their father. However, such differences can also be caused by indirect parental genetic effects, i.e. the fact that the genotype of a parent can be associated with behavioral or environmental changes that affect the phenotype of their offspring. No study of the human methylome has so far accounted for this confounding effect when inferring imprinted loci. Here, we jointly estimate direct, maternal, paternal and parent-of-origin effects at 850,055 methylation probes from whole blood in 2,438 parent-offspring trios from Generation Scotland. Of 5,435 probes with apparent POE signal, 4,974 (91.5%) fall below threshold once parental genotypes are included, suggesting that the vast majority are not attributable to imprinting alone. We treat the 281 remaining probes, 17 on the X chromosome and 42 not previously reported, as a conservative, high-confidence set, map them to 1,118 SNP loci linked to gene expression and protein abundance, and identify 27 probes where imprinting and indirect parental genetic effects both contribute. In a hold-out set of relatives, 250 of the 281 show familial resemblance consistent with a combination of imprinting and parental effects. Our results highlight the importance of accounting for indirect parental genetic effects when interpreting putative imprinting regions.

papers.title: Convergent Genomic Signatures of Selection in Thar: Genetic trade-offs for desert survival
papers.abstract: Background: Desert environments provide a setting for natural biological experiments to cope up with simultaneous stressors of extreme temperatures, aridity, UV exposure, and limited food resources. Biological adaptations that support living in such an environment could become liabilities when the environment and lifestyle change due to gene-environment mismatch. We explored whether genetically and culturally diverse endogamous native populations of the Thar exhibit convergent signatures of selection to desert conditions and whether the selected loci have implications in traits and disease susceptibilities relevant to non-native transitions. Results: We report 348 high-confidence variants across 45 candidate genes from a study on 176 individuals from eight genetically distinct Thar populations. These genes identified from humans and other desert inhabitants display convergent evolution with multiple selection scans (PBSn1, Tajima`s D, iHS, and XPEHH) in diverse Thar populations. Prominent genes include ZNF385D, SGCZ, SARDH, SLC12A3, etc. Selected variants essential in the desert environment were associated with complex traits like lipid metabolism, hypertension, renal and cardiovascular diseases, and addiction in GWAS and PheWAS. Noteworthy, in a syntenic locus, eQTLs in SARDH, which modulates DBH implicated in addiction, suggest a potential link with survival advantage in an uncertain desert environment. Likewise, a selected variant (rs7204044) in SLC12A3, implicated in hypertension in non-desert populations, seems to be a key to water-salt homeostasis in desert natives. Conclusions: These findings suggest that variants linked to adaptive traits in desert conditions could be linked to maladaptation in an altered environment. This has potential health consequences in climatic and lifestyle transitions among native inhabitants.

papers.title: The Caenorhabditis elegans pangenome elucidates hyper-divergent region gene content to reveal extensive gene copy-number variation and a novel anthelmintic resistance locus
papers.abstract: Caenorhabditis elegans has been a keystone model in biological research since the early 1970s, and it was the first metazoan to have its genome sequenced and assembled in 1998. Over the last few decades, the genetic and genomic resources developed for C. elegans made it one of the most powerful models for understanding metazoan biology. Recently, the C. elegans community has collected over 2,000 globally distributed wild strains, which after whole-genome sequencing, were found to contain punctuated regions of extreme genetic variation, called hyper-divergent regions (HDRs). HDRs have been described in organisms across the tree of life, including plants and humans, and genes in HDRs appear to be involved in adaptation, such as environmental response genes, parasitism genes, or immunity genes. However, the extreme genetic divergence at these loci complicates short-read alignments, and the genomic content of these regions in non-reference strains is largely uncharacterized. To define the gene content in HDRs, we de novo assembled and annotated genomes of 140 genetically diverse strains. These data enabled the construction of the first gene-based pangenome for the species. Among these strains, we characterized the landscape of structural variation and developed novel methods to quantify gene content diversity. We found that both variable copy-number and stable-copy environmental response genes were enriched in HDRs. These results further suggest that these regions have an important evolutionary role in adaptation to heterogeneous environments. We leveraged this pangenome to elucidate gene content in previously identified quantitative trait loci associated with adaptive traits. In one HDR, we found large deletions, spanning multiple genes, that are correlated with resistance to the anthelmintic drug abamectin. The C. elegans pangenome provides novel insights into genome and gene family evolution in a genetically diverse animal species, and empowers deeper investigations of genotype-phenotype relationships underlying adaptive traits, particularly in the context of structural and gene copy-number variation.

papers.title: A compartmentalised cochlear ageing programme: weak systemic concordance and a distinct macrophage compartment
papers.abstract: Whether the ageing cochlea follows the systemic ageing programmes defined by multi-organ atlases is unknown. We integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data for 13,988 mouse cochlear nuclei (3, 12 and 24 months) with the Tabula Muris Senis atlas (16 droplet-based and 12 Smart-seq2 fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) sources). Cross-organ alignment of ageing programmes was quantified by genome-wide vector correlation, pre-ranked gene-set enrichment and a systemic ageing score. Cochlear ageing showed weak but significant genome-wide concordance with systemic ageing (Spearman rho 0.01-0.12), with lineage-matched pairs ranking among the highest. In contrast, systemic tissue ageing-up signatures, dominated by immune and inflammatory programmes, were depleted from the ageing-up rankings of cochlear non-sensory epithelial cells (normalised enrichment score -1.45, adjusted p = 0.032) and, for the immune-organ signatures, from cochlear macrophages. The cochlear macrophage ageing vector correlated positively with tissue-resident macrophages of peripheral organs (kidney rho = 0.056, 95% confidence interval 0.016-0.063, p = 1.6 x 10^-13; microglia rho = 0.034, p = 1.4 x 10^-6), negatively with bone-marrow and splenic macrophages, and not with lymphocytes. A systemic ageing score increased with age in spiral ganglion neurons, Schwann cells, inner hair cells, epithelial cells, and fibrocytes, but not in cochlear macrophages. These cell-type-resolved analyses support a compartmentalised view of cochlear ageing: non-immune compartments track systemic ageing weakly, the immune arm is reversed, and cochlear macrophages age along a tissue-resident rather than haematopoietic programme.

papers.title: Transposase-mediated activity is associated with accessory gene turnover and positive-selection signals in Streptococcus pyogenes
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree. A GenomegaMap scan identified 163 of 3,147 genes with {omega} > 1. These genes were depleted among core genes and enriched among cloud genes, a pattern consistent with positive selection on recently acquired genes but also with the retention of slightly deleterious variation in young genes. A putative IS transposase (K07497) was the most consistent functional enrichment signal, which led us to analyze insertion sequence (IS) elements directly. In group 12, complete IS copies within genomes were more often near-identical than in other groups (OR = 1.46), consistent with more recent IS activity, and genes with {omega} > 1 were 2.9 times more likely than other accessory genes to lie within 5 kb of an IS element (8.8% vs. 3.0%; permutation p = 0.0006) after excluding IS-encoded genes. We did not detect this association in any other group, and most genes under selection were not IS-proximal.

papers.title: The assembly and annotation of a new reference genome for the eastern mosquitofish (Gambusia holbrooki) reveal a new sex chromosome system in its invasive range
papers.abstract: Gambusia species, especially eastern mosquitofish - Gambusia holbrooki - are of broad relevance to evolutionary biologists aiming at understanding genomic bases of adaptation during biological invasions and rapid response to selection to heterogeneous environments including pollution. Here we used HiFi and HiC to assemble a new, high quality, chromosome scale, genome sequence for G. holbrooki in its invasive range. Both haplotypes of the nuclear genome were assembled, comprising 657.64 Mb and 651.75 Mb respectively, in 24 chromosomes and had N50s of 28.97 Mb and 28.25 Mb. They had 94.87% and 94.29% BUSCO scores, illustrating a high completeness. Genome annotation yielded 25146 genes, which is comparable to other recent genome annotations of poecilid fish species. Repeat content was 25.69%, similar to what was previously reported for this species and for G. affinis. Synteny was highly conserved between the G. holbrooki assembly and the reference genome for G. affinis and Xiphophorus maculatus, shown here to be a genetically close species, with very few inter-chromosomal and little intra-chromosomal rearrangements. Mapping of resequenced males and females to the reference genome provided genomic evidence for a newly evolved homomorphic sex chromosome pair (W and Z, hence with female heterogamety) in G. holbrooki's invaded range, which is unlike the XY system of its native range. Also, the new sex chromosomes are homologous to the ZW sex chromosome pair (chromosome 1) of the sister species G. affinis. This assembly provides a high quality reference genome for Gambusia holbrooki, in its invasive range in Europe, that is serving as a key resource for research on the genomics of invasion and of rapid adaptation to environmental change, pollution adaptation and sex determination evolution.

papers.title: MARRI: Mechanism-Aware Learning of RNA-RNA Interactions with Foundation Models
papers.abstract: RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs) are central to post-transcriptional regulation, yet their prediction requires accounting for structural accessibility and intermolecular base pairing beyond sequence complementarity. Pretrained RNA foundation models provide representations of individual RNAs, but translating these representations into interaction predictions requires mechanistic knowledge of interaction recognition. Here, we introduce MARRI, a mechanism-aware multimodal framework that couples pretrained representations with domain knowledge by embedding learned opening penalties and hybridization gains into bidirectional cross-RNA attention. MARRI improves ROC--AUC and PR--AUC over the strongest baseline by 12.20% and 10.25%, respectively, and maintains strong discrimination for unseen RNA partnerships and interaction regions. Perturbation and repeat-context analyses identify prediction-relevant sequence regions. Integrating MARRI-derived interaction propensities with disease-associated expression profiles links molecular prediction to systems-level models of disease progression and network remodeling. MARRI thus illustrates a knowledge-guided strategy for coupling molecular foundation models with domain knowledge to support grounded prediction, interpretation and systems-level hypothesis generation.

papers.title: Comparative metagenomics reveals diversity and metabolic heterogeneity of sediment microbes from the Great Barrier Reef
papers.abstract: Microbial communities in coral reefs are highly connected through benthic-pelagic coupling. Pelagic and host-associated microbiomes have recently been characterised via genome-resolved metagenomics. However, similar characterisation of sediment communities has lagged behind due to their higher complexity. Here, using short- and long-read shotgun sequence data, we characterised sediment microbial communities of Australia's Great Barrier Reef. From 191 samples across 48 broadly distributed sites, we recovered 2,698 prokaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) representing 1,201 species-level clusters, most of which are novel. Compared against their sympatric counterparts in seawater, sediment MAGs exhibited greater phylogenetic diversity and flexibility in metabolic potential, implicating diverse respiration strategies and cycling of nitrogen, sulphur, and hydrogen. They also encode more abundant and novel biosynthetic capabilities, likely reflecting competition and adaptation to intermittent fluctuations in nutrient regimes, and between oxic and anoxic conditions. Our results provide foundational genomic resources for reef sediment microbes, uncovering biodiversity and function that together with planktonic microbes shape the ecological success and stability of coral reef ecosystems.

papers.title: Multimodal Structural and Regulatory Architecture of Coding and Non-Coding Variants Across the Orofacial Clefting TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 Network
papers.abstract: Pathogenic variation across the TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 transcriptional network causes syndromic and nonsyndromic orofacial clefts (OFCs), yet scalar sequence predictors collapse distinct failure modes and leave isoform-specific coding variants, splice-altering indels, and distal enhancer alleles unresolved. Here, we integrate 29 AlphaFold 3 (AF3) assemblies (10 wild-type, 19 mutant), thermodynamic stability ({Delta}{Delta}G) calculations, and AlphaGenome regulatory modeling across clinical, saturation-mutagenesis, and reporter benchmarks. In strict leave-one-gene-out (LOGO) coding benchmarks, replacing paralog crystal templates with full-length human AF3 structures improves IRF6 classification (biophysical AUROC rising from 0.7844 to 0.8967; {Delta}{Delta}G from 0.6461 to 0.8516) and resolves canonical isoform gaps in the 602-residue MANE Select GRHL3 homodimer. Projecting IRF6 missense variants onto a two-dimensional stability-versus-interface phase plane separates dominant-negative popliteal pterygium syndrome (PPS) poisons from haploinsufficient Van der Woude syndrome (VWS1) alleles (VWS1-versus-PPS Quadrant I odds ratio [OR] = 0.0263 [reciprocal OR = 38.0], p = 4.652 x 10-3) and distinguishes DNA-contact poisons from dimer-unfolding alleles across 12 zebrafish in vivo assays. Atomistic base-readout contacts in the AF3 TP63-MCS9.7 tetramer mirror loss-of-function profiles in MaveDB ({rho} = 0.6048, p = 6.52 x 10-4) and AlphaGenome keratinocyte DNase predictions ({rho} = 0.6040, p = 6.65 x 10-4). Across non-coding benchmarks, AlphaGenome splicing tracks reach an AUROC of 0.9876 while prioritizing cryptic splice variants of uncertain significance, and epithelial chromatin tracks capture enhancer grammar, plasmid-cloning artifacts, and context-dependent ARHGAP29, FOXE1, and local 8q24 chromatin effects within AlphaGenome's 1.049-Mb horizon.

papers.title: Target-enrichment sequencing reveals intergenotypic reassortment of infectious salmon anaemia virus in Atlantic Canada
papers.abstract: Infectious salmon anaemia virus (ISAV) causes severe disease and substantial economic losses in farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar). The virus has an eight-segment, negative-sense single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) genome and is divided into European and North American genotypes. Despite their co-circulation in locations such as the Atlantic coast of Canada, reassortment between these genotypes has never been observed. However, routine diagnostic and sequence-based surveillance often target individual genome segments and may therefore fail to identify reassortant viruses or accurately resolve their genomic ancestry. In this study, we developed a probe panel targeting both genotypes and applied Oxford Nanopore sequencing to 37 ISAV-positive samples collected from 14 farm sites in the Bay of Fundy, New Brunswick, Canada. Twenty-seven samples yielded 29 consensus genomes, including separate viral consensuses recovered from two mixed infections. Segment-specific phylogenies identified 24 viruses with a previously unreported intergenotypic genomic constellation comprising a European-genotype segment 3 and North American-genotype segments 1, 2 and 4 - 8. Their consistent monophyletic clustering across segment-specific phylogenies supports a single ancestral reassortment event followed by onward circulation of the reassortant lineage. A time-scaled phylogeny of segment 3 estimated the posterior mean time to the most recent common ancestor (tMRCA) of the sampled reassortant cluster as September 2016 (95% HPD: March 2013-June 2019), indicating that this segment 3 lineage pre-dated its first sampling in 2021. Five additional viruses represented several distinct EU-genotype lineages. To our knowledge, this is the first documented reassortment between the European and North American ISAV genotypes. These findings identify an intergenotypic reassortant lineage detected across multiple farms in the Bay of Fundy and demonstrate the value of whole-genome sequencing for detecting reassortment, mixed infections and epidemiologically relevant viral diversity.

papers.title: ChIMe-seq enables multimodal epigenetic profiling in single molecules and single cells
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell and single-molecule sequencing have enabled high-resolution characterization of epigenetic states. However, methods that jointly measure multiple layers of epigenetic regulation within the same molecules and cells remain limited. Here, we developed Chromatin Immuno-Methylation sequencing (ChIMe-seq), a multimodal approach that simultaneously profiles histone modifications, DNA methylation, and nucleosome positioning genome-wide in single molecules and single cells. In contrast to recent approaches that rely on enzymatic fragmentation, ChIMe-seq preserves long DNA molecules by using a methyltransferase to deposit exogenous methylation marks that report on proximal histone modifications. This enables integration of multiple epigenetic features within individual molecules and supports short-read, long-read, and single-cell sequencing. These multimodal measurements are integrated into a novel mathematical framework that captures the coupling between nucleosome positioning, histone modifications, and DNA methylation. Both single-molecule and single-cell analyses reveal that DNA methylation is linked to nucleosome density in a manner modulated by local histone modifications, whilst differences in nucleosome:DNA structures are observed depending on epigenetic context and cell-type. Together, these results establish ChIMe-seq as a framework to investigate multifaceted epigenetic coordination across scales, from single-nucleotide resolution to long-range chromatin organization in single molecules and single cells.

papers.title: Genome assembly for Amanita muscaria var. muscaria
papers.abstract: Amanita muscaria is a charismatic and widely distributed mushroom-forming fungus. Amanita muscaria comprises a species complex, and genomic resources are unevenly distributed, which may bias genetic and genomic study of the species complex. This study produces a high quality hybrid genome assembly of a specimen from New Zealand. Phylogenetic analysis shows that this belongs to Amanita muscaria var. muscaria.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal profiling reveals emergence of cell type-specific molecular aging and senescence programs in the spinal cord
papers.abstract: The spinal cord is the primary relay center between the periphery and the brain, playing a critical role in sensory, motor and autonomic function. Despite its functional importance, the cellular and molecular changes underlying spinal cord aging and their relationship to cellular senescence - a hallmark associated with aging - remain incompletely understood. Here, we generated a cross-species, multi-omic atlas of spinal cord aging in mice and humans by integrating a combination of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, Visium spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing, and multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging. We identified converging age-associated increases in fibrinogen, laminin, and immune activation-associated proteins across the mouse and human spinal cord. Over the mouse lifespan, we further identified distinct spatiotemporal patterns of aging. Downregulated transcriptional programs, including synaptic signaling, mitochondrion organization, and autophagy, were most highly expressed in grey matter regions and in neurons. Upregulated transcriptional programs, including vascular and immune processes, were enriched in white matter regions and in endothelial cells and microglia, respectively. Notably, these increasing spatial modules were also enriched for senescence-associated genes. In the human spinal cord, endothelial cells and microglia were also most enriched for canonical senescence markers CDKN1A and CDKN2A, respectively. Overall, this study defines the shared, spatially-resolved, cell type-specific features associated with aging and senescence in the mouse and human spinal cord.

papers.title: Computable Genomes: A Layered Computational Framework for Non-Coding DNA and Cellular Behavior
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies have catalogued tens of thousands of trait-associated loci, most of them in non-coding DNA, yet for most loci the path from nucleotide to phenotype remains correlational. We propose a layered computational decomposition of the genome as a complement to data-driven approaches: sequence as formal language, sequence as information-bearing signal, mobile elements as runtime, compilation to interaction networks through thermodynamic and rule-based models, and execution as cellular and multicellular dynamics. Each layer is defined by its inputs, outputs and formalisms, and we set out where the frame breaks down, including the looseness of algorithmic-information estimates, the triviality of universality results and the failure of string grammars at the chromatin level. Synthetic-biology platforms serve as tests of whether the layers compose, and genomic foundation models and the AlphaGenome Atlas, which predicts effects for all nine billion possible single-nucleotide variants, serve as oracles whose coverage and limits we map onto the framework. We state five falsifiable predictions and test the first, that sequence compressibility carries information about regulatory function beyond composition and conservation, on 38,556 single-nucleotide variants from a saturation-mutagenesis reporter assay of 21 regulatory elements. In a pooled model, local compressibility is associated with measured effect size (standardized {beta} = -0.030, p = 0.0014). The association roughly halves under full control for base composition, loses significance when composition, motif and noise adjustments are combined under locus-level inference (wild cluster bootstrap p = 0.11), and averages zero within loci (random-effects {beta} = -0.0003, p = 0.90). The prediction is therefore not supported at the variant level in these data, which bound the effect a genome-wide test should expect. The argument is not that the genome "is" a program, but that treating it as one supplies formal tools whose predictions can be checked.

papers.title: A de novo reference genome of the red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis
papers.abstract: Furcellaria lumbricalis is a red seaweed that occurs across a broad salinity gradient, ranging from the saline waters of the NE Atlantic to the brackish Baltic Sea. In the Baltic Sea, natural populations of F. lumbricalis are harvested commercially, primarily for furcellaran extraction, a sulphated polysaccharide used as a stabilizing, thickening, and gelling agent. Genomic resources for this species remain absent, constraining evolutionary, ecological, and applied research. Here, we present a de novo reference genome assembly of the seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis using PacBio Hifi and Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read sequencing. The final assembly, consisting of 149 contigs spanning 918.2 Mb, contains a high proportion of repetitive elements (90.5%), and has an N50 of 15,5 Mb. We further integrated RNA-seq data, protein homology evidence, and ab initio gene prediction to build a genome annotation comprising 6100 genes, of which 82.6% has a functional annotation. This genomic evidence contributes to a steadily growing body of genomic resources of red algae, with often expanded and highly repetitive genomes, and helps facilitate the study of genetic adaptation to their unique environments.

papers.title: Regulatory grammar design of tissue-specific enhancers across species
papers.abstract: Enhancers encode tissue-specific gene expression through the combinatorial identity, number, and arrangement of transcription factor motifs, collectively known as regulatory grammar. However, existing deep-learning methods directly optimize nucleotide sequences, leaving enhancer regulatory grammar implicit. Here we introduce REgulatory Grammar Architecture via reinforcement Learning (REGAL), a framework that explicitly programs enhancer grammar under sequence-to-function oracles. REGAL generated tissue-specific enhancers across species using the same placement architecture with interchangeable oracles and motif vocabularies. Experimental validation and perturbation revealed that tissue specificity requires coordinated target-tissue activation and off-target repression, depends on both motif composition and spatial organization, and employs distinct regulatory strategies across tissues. REGAL-designed enhancers drove predicted lineage-specific expression in transgenic mouse embryos, outperformed a nucleotide-level optimizer in human cells, and matched or exceeded leading designs in zebrafish and Drosophila at notably shorter length. Together, these findings establish regulatory grammar as a programmable and experimentally testable substrate underlying enhancer design and specificity.

papers.title: Fine-tuned DNA sequence language models for predicting gene expression in admixed population: A comparison with variant-based methods
papers.abstract: Predicting gene expression from whole genome sequencing data is essential for elucidating regulatory mechanisms and interpreting functional consequences of non-coding variants to complex diseases. While traditional approaches rely on variant-based linear models, DNA sequence-based language models have gained increasing popularity for their ability to learn regulatory features directly from whole genome sequence data. Previous studies have evaluated models such as Enformer, but newer sequence-to-function models, including Borzoi and AlphaGenome, remain less well characterized for individual-level gene expression prediction, particularly in non-European and admixed populations. Here, we evaluated and fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome using personal genomes paired with whole-blood RNA-seq data from the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL). Fine-tuning substantially improved the performance of both sequence-based models compared with their pretrained versions; however, their performances remained similar to that of the variant-based linear models. Leveraging the ancestral diversity of HCHS/SOL, we found that Borzoi and AlphaGenome showed similar performance across Amerindian-, European-, and African-enriched groups. Fine-tuned Borzoi, fine-tuned AlphaGenome and elastic net performed modestly better when trained and evaluated in the same ancestry-enriched group. Finally, we explored strategies to improve prediction performance and found that incorporating predicted epigenetic features improved prediction near the promoter region. Significant progress remains needed before the full potential of sequence-based models is attained. Incorporating more biology-guided training approaches could be helpful to achieving better performance.

papers.title: FULL-seq reveals isoform-specific regulatory architecture in single cells
papers.abstract: Gene regulation is commonly modeled at the gene level, yet genes express multiple isoforms from distinct transcription start sites whose regulatory architecture is not resolved by current approaches. Here we introduce FULL-seq, a scalable single-cell multiomic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and full-length transcript coverage from the same cell, enabling direct coupling of regulatory elements to alternative first exon (AFE) usage. FULL-seq achieves high sensitivity for both transcriptome and chromatin accessibility while providing transcript-wide coverage across mRNAs up to 15 kb with precise exon-level mapping. We uncover diverse promoter-AFE regulatory architectures, revealing distinct transcription factor programs across alternative first exons of the same gene, and show that gene-level annotation frameworks can obscure regulatory relationships in multi-promoter genes. Applying FULL-seq to human cancer cells further reveals metastasis-associated AFE programs that are not apparent from gene-level expression. These AFE programs were reproduced in independent colorectal cancer cell-line datasets, and CALB1 AFE activation was observed in a subset of liver metastases from an independent patient cohort. Furthermore, CRISPRi-mediated repression of metastasis-associated CALB1 AFEs reduced colorectal cancer cell migration. Together, our findings establish alternative promoter and first-exon usage as a functionally relevant layer of gene regulation and demonstrate that FULL-seq enables regulatory relationships and cellular phenotypes to be connected at the promoter-isoform level.

papers.title: De novo Genome Assembly and Annotation of the Seep Tubeworm Lamellibrachia satsuma using Oxford Nanopore Sequencing
papers.abstract: The tubeworm Lamelllibrachia satsuma inhabits seep region by forming a mutualistic symbiotic relationship with chemosynthetic bacteria residing in its trophosome. Genomic and symbiotic studies have been extensively conducted, primarily from a bacterial perspective. But rarely vice versa. Here we present a high-quality draft genome assembly of L. satsuma and its tissue-specific transcriptome data. This genome will be valuable for further understanding the mechanisms of adaptation in cold seep environments, host-microbe interactions, as well as genome variation among tubeworms. We generated ~103 Gb of genomic sequencing data using Illumina and Oxford Nanopore platforms, which assembled in a 665 Mb draft genome. The assembled genome consisted of 6,320 scaffolds with 95.7% genome completeness. Among 32,394 predicted protein-coding genes, 1,063 gene families have expanded, and 1,385 gene families were contracted. Among the expanded gene families, multiple copies of leukocyte elastase inhibitor, reverse transcriptase, arylesterase, and xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase genes were found. Molecular clock analysis based on the phylogenomic dataset revealed that L. sastuma and L. luymesi were diverged from their common ancestor during the Early Cenozoic era, approximately 13 million years ago.

papers.title: Robust Cluster Typing, a computationally accessible tool for species designation from whole genome data, exemplified with the genus Campylobacter
papers.abstract: Bacterial genomic analysis is a cornerstone of modern epidemiology. Many genomic typing methods exist, and most are designed to work within a given species in a hierarchical fashion. However, designation of bacterial species can be problematic, making the higher resolution level of hierarchical typing difficult. Using the universally present ribosomal proteins, we have developed a pipeline for a robust typing system which can be used to assign an unknown organism to a species-level cluster or, sometimes, a sub-species cluster. As proof of principle, we have used bacterial genomes from the genus Campylobacter, the most common cause of human bacterial gastroenteritis within which new strains, and new species (C. infantis), are reported. Species assignment, of all but the two most common species C. jejuni and C. coli, is beyond the ability of most microbiology laboratories. Outbreak investigation, even with genomic data, is difficult and so a robust typing scheme would be useful. Using available sequence-based typing schemes, we attempted to differentiate between 39 published Campylobacter species; we determined that the ribosomal 16S sequence typing and SNP typing did not discriminate all 39 but a single gene phylogeny method (GyrA), BUSCO, Mash, Panaroo and use of the Hugg proteins differentiated all 39. We assessed computational accessibility (important for implementation) and biological applicability (one universal typing scheme is easier to validate). The application of Hugg proteins proved computationally efficient and should be widely applicable. We developed a workflow in snakemake and Python, capable of clustering thousands of bacterial genomes. This Robust Cluster (RC) typing workflow was made accessible via the Terra platform, with usage instructions provided through an online training course on YouTube. Ninety-eight Campylobacter isolates from Bangladesh were sequenced and analysed using the Terra workflow, resulting in the identification of several novel clusters not previously found among publicly available genomes. Our work establishes the availability of RC typing and demonstrates its capacity to identify new Campylobacter lineages, thereby facilitating reporting and supporting future research initiatives.

papers.title: No detectable DNA methylation in the kelps (Laminariales): a conversion-free test of a predicted loss
papers.abstract: Kelps (Laminariales) dominate temperate and polar rocky coasts and support a fast-growing aquaculture sector. Breeding and restoration programs need to know whether a line's performance follows its genotype or its culture history. DNA methylation has been reported in kelps, with differences by life stage, thermal history and population of origin now underpinning a literature on conditioning and priming in seaweed breeding. Recent comparative genomics work predicts otherwise, because brown algae lack the canonical DNA methyltransferases and should therefore carry little or no DNA methylation. We tested the prediction with native-DNA nanopore sequencing, which requires neither bisulfite conversion nor methylation-dependent digestion, in seven kelp datasets spanning three genera, four species and four S. latissima life stages. Nuclear 5-methylcytosine stayed at the measurement background in every sequence context (CG 0.021-0.034% of sites, against 0.023% on PCR copies that carry no methyl group by construction), while the same pipeline returned 58% of CG sites methylated in a diatom and recovered the transposon-targeted distribution a functioning system predicts. In native reads, thirteen of the fourteen best-covered chloroplast positions that bisulfite sequencing placed above 2% carry at most one methylated call, and those published levels track each library's conversion efficiency rather than its tissue. Gene content and direct measurement agree, so the heritable effects reported in cultivated kelp require a carrier other than DNA methylation: chromatin modifications or non-coding RNA.

papers.title: Dynamics of somatic L1 retrotransposition in the human brain
papers.abstract: The sole source of genomic diversity in the human brain caused by autonomous retrotransposition is facilitated by the long interspersed nuclear element-1 (L1). However, assessing the rate, timing and source elements of this event has been challenging due to the lack of technologies that capture of L1s at sufficient scale in single cells. Here, we introduce LUSTRE, a single-cell assay that enables mapping L1 sites without whole-genome amplification, and profile ~17,600 neurons from the dentate gyrus, cortex, cerebellum of the adult human brain. We report the presence of somatic L1s that define related lineages and conservatively estimate a validation-adjusted rate of 0.1-0.3 somatic events per neuron. Our analyses further indicate two distinct waves of retrotransposition during development and combined with the variability in their polyA tract lengths across single nuclei, suggest the formation of lineage hierarchies marked by new somatic retrotransposition events and cell divisions. Mapping the origin of L1s through 3'-transduction events identify the rare source L1s that are responsible for the majority of retrotransposition events. These results uncover the dynamics of L1-driven somatic mosaicism and establish L1s as endogenous recorders of cellular and lineage history in human tissues.

papers.title: pbzarr: cohort-scale storage and analysis of per-base genomic data with Zarr
papers.abstract: Genomic assays now produce per-base signals for cohorts comprising thousands of samples. However, existing genomic data storage formats (e.g., D4, bigWig) were designed primarily for single samples or individual datasets. Consequently, cohort-scale analyses across samples, populations, or species require opening, reading, and merging thousands of files before proceeding to downstream computational analyses. Here, we present pbzarr, a format and toolkit that stores per-base genomic data from many samples and assays as a single Zarr store. Across multiple datasets, pbzarr simplified cohort construction to a single command and created cohort-scale datasets up to 2.1x faster than existing approaches while simultaneously using 5-6x less memory. More importantly, pbzarr compresses signal tracks to only a fraction of the input data size, using only 3.3% of the input size to store per-base coverage for 1,024 short-read genomes. Despite this smaller storage footprint, pbzarr maintains fast access to underlying genomic data: region-based queries complete 61x faster than D4 and 6x faster than bigWig, and full-genome scans are as fast or faster than existing formats. Finally, because pbzarr stores are native Zarr arrays, it integrates directly with widely used array libraries (e.g., Xarray and Dask), allowing cohort-scale analyses to be expressed in a single line of Python code using standard array operations instead of a complex, custom pipeline. Together, our results suggest that pbzarr is dramatically smaller, substantially simpler, and faster than competing formats for biobank-scale analysis. pbzarr is open source and available at https://github.com/pbzarr/pbzarr.

papers.title: Contrasting plasmid-host associations shape the distribution of enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) colonization factors
papers.abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) causes a substantial burden of diarrhoeal disease, but how its virulence plasmids spread across E. coli populations remains unclear. We generated 479 complete ETEC genomes and combined them with 56 publicly available assemblies to produce the largest plasmid-resolved ETEC collection to date. Clustering of 903 virulence plasmids identified distinct plasmid lineages associated with individual colonization factors (CFs). Some CFs were carried by plasmids confined to a single ETEC lineage, consistent with long-term vertical maintenance, whereas others, including CS23 and CS12, were found on closely related conjugative plasmids distributed across multiple lineages, indicating horizontal transfer. Screening the AllTheBacteria dataset confirmed these patterns and revealed additional plasmid diversity for several CFs. Finally, we identified eight previously undescribed putative adhesion operons on toxin plasmids that may explain CF-negative ETEC isolates. These findings showed that plasmids, rather than bacterial lineages alone, shape the evolution and dissemination of ETEC virulence.

papers.title: The genetic regulation of thyroid hormones on immune and hematopoietic homeostasis: an integrative Mendelian randomization and colocalization study
papers.abstract: Background: Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. Methods: We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effects of 25 genetically predicted hematological traits on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the UK Biobank. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were selected as instrumental variables and harmonized before analysis. Causal estimates were primarily obtained using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method and complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, simple mode, MR-PRESSO, and MR-robust adjusted profile score (MR-RAPS) analyses. Sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, reverse causality, and directionality. Significant findings were replicated using independent FinnGen summary statistics. Multivariable MR and Bayesian colocalization analyses were subsequently performed to investigate significant associations further. Results: Among the 25 hematological traits evaluated, eosinophil-related traits showed the strongest associations with hypothyroidism. Genetically predicted eosinophil counts were associated with an increased risk of hypothyroidism (odds ratio [OR] = 1.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11-1.42, P = 4.0E-04, FDR = 0.002), while combined eosinophil-basophil counts showed similar associations (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.10-1.40, P = 5.0E-04, FDR = 0.002). These findings were consistently replicated in FinnGen and remained significant after adjustment for basophil traits, body mass index, and C-reactive protein in multivariable MR analyses. No significant associations were observed for hyperthyroidism. Bayesian colocalization identified strong evidence of a shared genetic signal at the rs653178 locus on chromosome 12 (PP.H4 = 0.994). Conclusions: This study provides genetic evidence supporting a causal role for eosinophil-related traits in hypothyroidism susceptibility. The consistency of the findings across complementary Mendelian randomization approaches, independent replication, multivariable analyses, and colocalization strengthens the evidence that eosinophil-related immune mechanisms contribute to hypothyroidism susceptibility.
